newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ruling party threatens secularism - Turk prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party threatens secularism - Turk prosecutor.

text.p: A top prosecutor has called on the constitutional court to outlaw Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party for threatening the secularist Turkish state, according to a charge sheet seen by Reuters on Wednesday.
But a cabinet minister from the Islam-based Welfare said he was confident the party would weather the latest storm.
"It has become clear that (Welfare) has become a focus of actions contrary to the principle of secularism in the constitution," the charge sheet read.

Prosecutor Vural Savas, the head of the republican appeals court prosecutorial office, said earlier he had demanded that the constitutional court outlaw the Welfare, the first Islamist party to lead officially secular Turkey.
"It has pushed our country towards a civil war atmosphere," said the charge sheet.
Ahmet Cemil Tunc, a Welfare minister of state, dismissed the charges and said the party remained well within the bounds of Turkish democracy.
"Our party will not be closed. It is not possible because our party has always worked for freedom and democracy," Tunc told Reuters.
Welfare has upset the secularist establishment, led by the powerful army, with plans for mild Islamist reforms since it came to office in coalition with the secularist True Path Party last June.
Their alliance narrowly survived an opposition censure motion on Tuesday.
Istanbul stocks, normally highly sensitive to Turkey's political instability, were up one percent in mid-morning trading.
